SAQ2.question: Over the course of years between 2009 and 2014, the number of girls named 'Isla' was always more than 'Amelia'. True or False?
SAQ2.reference_chain: SCAN({xtick 2009..2014}) → for each x: SEG(top(band[Isla]) − top(band[Amelia])) vs READ(top(band[Amelia]), y) → e.g. @2012: SEG(10500 − 7000)≈3500 < 7000 → CMP(Isla < Amelia @2009..2013) → ANSWER(False)
SAQ2.notes: The pivotal confusion is between stack position and band thickness. Most participants traced the top edges of the purple and orange bands and concluded 'Isla is always above Amelia', which is True only by position. The 8 correct responders used thickness, through brackets or double arrows spanning each band at 2009/2012/2014 (P42, P56, P72), or through a holistic 'more orange area' judgement (P53, P65). Several participants knew the encoding was stacked ('Isla's numbers also include Amelia's', 'each colour represents the surplus') yet still compared tops. Two declared the chart unanswerable, and one read peak heights (~10500 vs ~7000) straight off the y-axis.
